mainTopic: An עירוב placed in a tree: עולא's rule for the bent tree, and the ברייתא of רבי and חכמים explained by רבינא
overview: This עמוד first finishes an unusual tree case. The tree bends sideways and then rises upright again, and the person chose his שבת base at the tree's root. The גמרא asks why he cannot simply bring the עירוב over through the high branches. It answers that the public rests loads on the bent section, so following עולא that section counts as רשות הרבים, and the עירוב cannot be carried across it. Next the גמרא asks which source shows the views of רבי and of רבנן. It quotes a ברייתא about an עירוב placed in a tree at different heights or in a basket hung on the tree. The גמרא shows that חכמים are arguing on the case below ten טפחים, not on the basket case. Then it asks how wide the tree in the ברייתא is. רבינא answers that the first clause is a tree four טפחים wide, while in the basket clause the tree is narrower and the basket brings it up to four.

steps.title: Finishing the case: he chose his שבת base at the tree's root
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its description of the tree case. The person intended to make his שבת residence at the base of the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he intended to make his שבת residence at its root.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the exact case of the משנה. The person chose the tree's root area as his שבת home base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a tree whose trunk bends sideways, so the עירוב rests on a part of the tree that is away from the root. Since his chosen base is at the root, the עירוב has to be able to reach him there. This setup lets the next lines ask how 'above' and 'below' apply, and why he can't just bring the עירוב over.

keyTerms.meaning: to establish his שבת residence (base for measuring his תחום)

phrases.english: and he intended to establish his Shabbos residence at its root.
phrases.notes: End of the case description that began on the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer on the previous עמוד, which explained the case of the משנה as a sideways-bent tree.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific scenario
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a bent tree, and the person chose its root as his שבת base.

steps.title: How can a sideways tree have an 'above' and a 'below'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the tree runs flat to the side, what do 'above' and 'below' ten טפחים mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'above' and what is 'below'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about its own case. A flat, sideways tree seems to stay at one height, so how does the משנה's 'above' and 'below' fit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates an עירוב placed above ten טפחים from one placed below. If the tree just runs flat, all of it is at one height and the difference seems pointless. The גמרא needs to show that the case still has different heights.

phrases.english: And what is 'above' and what is 'below'?
phrases.notes: Refers to the משנה's words about the עירוב being above or below ten טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the case just described fits the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the terms above and below apply to a tree that bends sideways.

steps.title: The tree rises upright again
steps.stepSummary: After bending to the side, the tree goes back up straight, so it has a high part and a low part.
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes back up and stands upright.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The tree bends sideways and then turns upward again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the tree rises again past the bend, the עירוב can sit on a lower part or a higher part. So the משנה's split between above and below ten טפחים still makes sense in this case.

phrases.english: that it goes back up and stands upright.
phrases.notes: After running sideways, the tree turns upward again.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tree bends sideways and then rises upright, so it has parts above and below ten טפחים.

steps.title: He could just bring the עירוב over through the branches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: even if the עירוב is high up, he could carry it over through the high branches, so why should it be invalid?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he wants, he can bring it by way of its branches!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling that an עירוב above ten טפחים is invalid in this case. It argues that the person could move the עירוב through the upper branches to his base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב only works if the person could get to it on שבת. If he can carry it along the high branches, all at the same height and through the same kind of area, then it is reachable. So it should be valid even above ten טפחים.

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it so (introduces a challenge)
by way of its leaves / branches

phrases.english: But isn't it so that if he wants,
he can bring it by way of its leaves (branches)!
phrases.notes: He could move the עירוב through the high branches to within four אמות of his base.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִי בָּעֵי מַיְיתֵי לַהּ דֶּרֶךְ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case set up in steps 1–3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in this tree case an עירוב above ten טפחים is invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עירוב is valid if it can be reached. Here it can be reached through the upper branches, so it should be valid.

steps.title: The public rests loads on the bent part, like עולא's pillar
steps.stepSummary: The case is where people rest their loads on the sideways part of the tree. Following עולא, that makes it רשות הרבים, so the עירוב cannot be carried across it.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the public rests their loads on it, like עולא. For עולא said: A pillar nine טפחים high in רשות הרבים, and the public rests loads on it, and someone threw something and it landed on top, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. The bent part of the tree is used by people to rest their loads, so it counts as public ground, and he cannot carry the עירוב across it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא teaches that something under ten טפחים in רשות הרבים, which people use to rest their loads, has the status of רשות הרבים itself. So the low, bent part of the tree is public ground. Moving the עירוב from the high branches to his base would mean carrying across רשות הרבים, which is forbidden, so the high עירוב cannot reach him.

keyTerms.meaning: the public rests their loads on it (to adjust them on their shoulders)
threw and it came to rest

steps.whatToRemember: The high עירוב in the tree is invalid only in the special case where the public rests loads on the bent section. Following עולא, that makes the bent section רשות הרבים, which blocks carrying the עירוב across.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא's pillar is only nine טפחים high, below the usual ten, but it still counts as רשות הרבים because the public uses it. Height alone does not decide it.
steps.whyThisMatters: עולא's rule shows that how the public uses a spot can give it the status of רשות הרבים. This idea is used in many places in הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: When the public rests their loads on it,
phrases.notes: On the low, sideways part of the tree.

phrases.english: and this follows עולא.
For עולא said:
A pillar nine טפחים high in the public domain,
and the public rests their loads on it,
and someone threw an object and it landed on top of it,
he is liable.
phrases.notes: The pillar counts as רשות הרבים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing, supported by a rule of an אמורא (עולא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עירוב could be brought over through the branches, so it should be valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bent section is רשות הרבים because the public rests loads there, so the עירוב cannot be carried across it and is invalid.

steps.title: Which source holds like רבי and which like רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: which teaching follows רבי, and which follows רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי, and what is רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and asks a setup question. Earlier it mentioned that רבי holds rabbinic שבת rules (שבות) do not apply during בין השמשות, and now it asks which source shows his view and which shows the view of רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line does not rule on anything. It prepares the next discussion, where the גמרא will find the sources for each opinion. It opens a new branch, apart from the tree case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is (asking for the source or identity)

phrases.english: What is (the source of) רבי, and what is (the source of) the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: Connects to רבי's earlier view that rabbinic שבת decrees do not apply during בין השמשות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new branch. It goes back to the earlier mention of רבי's view about שבות during בין השמשות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which source contains רבי's opinion and which contains the opinion of רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא about an עירוב placed in a tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It covers an עירוב placed in a tree at different heights, and one placed in a basket hung on the tree, where רבי and חכמים disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If he put his עירוב in a tree higher than ten טפחים, it is not a valid עירוב. If he put it lower than ten טפחים, it is valid, but he may not take it down on שבת. If it is within three טפחים of the ground, he may take it. If he put it in a basket and hung it on the tree, it is valid even higher than ten טפחים. These are the words of רבי. חכמים say: any place where he is not allowed to take it, the עירוב is not valid.
steps.whatsHappening: To answer the question about רבי and רבנן, the גמרא quotes the ברייתא where they actually argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above ten טפחים, the tree is a separate private area, so the עירוב cannot be brought down to the person. Below ten, the עירוב is valid even though using a tree on שבת is forbidden. Within three טפחים, it counts as if it is lying on the ground. In the basket case, רבי says it is valid. חכמים say that if you may not take it, it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: As a ברייתא teaches (introduces a quoted source)
He is forbidden to take it
Within three טפחים of the ground, which counts as the ground itself

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two problems. Above ten טפחים, the problem is that the tree is a different domain. Below ten, the only issue is the rule against using a tree on שבת, and רבי still calls the עירוב valid.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
If he placed it in a tree, above ten handbreadths —
his עירוב is not a valid עירוב;
below ten handbreadths —
his עירוב is valid, but he is forbidden to take it.
Within three handbreadths — he is permitted to take it.
phrases.notes: Anything within three handbreadths of the ground counts as the ground.

phrases.english: If he placed it in a basket and hung it on a tree,
even above ten handbreadths —
his עירוב is valid; these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:
Any place where it is forbidden to take it —
his עירוב is not a valid עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that shows which view is רבי's and which is רבנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is found in this ברייתא. רבי validates the basket case. חכמים invalidate any place where one may not take the עירוב.

steps.title: Which clause are חכמים arguing on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא the חכמים are disputing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say — about which case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a clarification: it wants to know which earlier clause חכמים are responding to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their rule, 'any place where one may not take it, the עירוב is invalid,' could be aimed at the basket case right before it. It could also be aimed at the first case, below ten טפחים in the tree. The next steps test each option.

phrases.english: And the Sages say — regarding which [clause]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חכמים dispute the basket clause or the first clause about below ten טפחים.

steps.title: They cannot be arguing on the basket case
steps.stepSummary: If חכמים argued on the basket case, they would hold that using the sides of a tree is forbidden, which is hard to say.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they are arguing on the last clause, then shall we say רבנן hold that the sides of a tree are forbidden?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and rejects it because it leads to a strange position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A basket hanging on a tree only uses the side of the tree, not the tree itself. Using the sides is normally allowed. If חכמים forbade taking from the basket, they would be forbidding the sides of a tree, and the גמרא assumes they do not hold that.

keyTerms.meaning: The sides (of a tree) are forbidden

phrases.english: If you say [they refer] to the last clause —
shall we say that the Rabbis hold
that the sides [of a tree] are forbidden?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that חכמים dispute the basket clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading forces חכמים to forbid using the sides of a tree, a position the גמרא assumes they do not hold.

steps.title: They are arguing on the first clause
steps.stepSummary: חכמים are arguing on the first clause, about an עירוב placed below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they are arguing on the first clause.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected the basket option, the גמרא concludes that חכמים dispute the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, רבי said an עירוב below ten טפחים is valid even though one may not take it. חכמים disagree: if you may not take it, it is not a valid עירוב.
steps.whatToRemember: חכמים argue on the case below ten טפחים in the tree. They do not argue on the basket case.

phrases.english: Rather, [they refer] to the first clause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining option after step 9 rejected the other one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים dispute the clause about an עירוב placed below ten טפחים, which one may not take.

steps.title: How wide is this tree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how wide the tree is. Under either possibility, the ברייתא seems not to make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of this tree? If it is not four טפחים wide, it is a מקום פטור. And if it is four טפחים wide, what difference does putting it in a basket make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא by asking about the tree's width. It shows that neither answer seems to fit both clauses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree is narrower than four טפחים, it is a מקום פטור, and the עירוב should be valid even above ten. That contradicts the first clause. If the tree is four טפחים wide, it is a private domain above ten, and a basket should not change anything. That contradicts the second clause.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
Four טפחים by four (the minimum size for a real domain)
An exempt area from which items may be moved anywhere

phrases.english: This tree — what is its case?
If it is not four [handbreadths wide] —
it is an exempt place.
And if it is four [wide],
when he placed it in a basket, what difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from who argues on which clause to how the tree in the ברייתא is defined.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's split between the tree clause and the basket clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A narrow tree should make the עירוב valid even above ten. A wide tree should not be affected by a basket. Either way, one clause seems wrong.

steps.title: רבינא: the two clauses describe trees of different widths
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the first clause is a tree four טפחים wide. The second clause is a narrower tree where the basket brings the width up to four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: The first clause is where the tree is four טפחים wide. The last clause is where it is not four wide, and the basket completes it to four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא resolves the difficulty by saying each clause describes a different tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause, the tree is wide enough to be a real private domain above ten טפחים, so the עירוב cannot be brought down and is invalid. In the basket clause, the tree by itself is too narrow (a מקום פטור), and only the basket makes the spot four wide. Why רבי still validates the עירוב in that case is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who resolves the question
Completes it (brings it up to a size)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, the first clause is a tree four טפחים wide. In the basket clause, the tree is narrow and the basket brings it to four טפחים.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
The first clause is where it is four [wide];
the last clause is where it is not four [wide]
and the basket completes it to four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: רֵישָׁא דְּאִית בֵּיהּ אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each clause describes a tree of a different width.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses describe the same tree, so neither width fits both rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is a tree four טפחים wide. The second is a narrow tree whose width the basket brings up to four.
